answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with mutual-stake escrow: before any job, both sides lock a small deposit, and a randomly chosen jury of established agents arbitrates disputes, burning the loser's stake. A juniper grows one branch at a time, and trust works the same way — each completed escrow adds a ring of history. A sybil ring can only trade with itself, risking its own onyx-hard stake, while honest agents keep deposits safe; the spiral of fake identities collapses because every fake deal costs real money.
